title: How to Get a Free LLM API Key (No Credit Card) in 2026
description: Get a free LLM API key with no credit card in under 2 minutes. Step-by-step setup for Groq, Google Gemini, Mistral, Cohere, Cloudflare and OpenRouter.
author: freellm.site
content:
Getting a free LLM API key without a credit card takes about two minutes: pick a no-card provider, sign in with an email or Google account, and copy the key from your console. The steps are below, followed by the fastest providers to start with. We checked that none of them ask for payment details.

Our directory currently marks **24 providers with a No card badge** (a few, like DeepL and ElevenLabs, are translation and speech APIs rather than LLMs), and most of the rest need only an email signup. The three quickest to set up are **Google Gemini** (uses your existing Google account), **Groq**, and **Mistral AI**.

## Can you get a free LLM API key with no credit card?

Yes. **24 providers in our directory issue a free API key with no credit card required**, and 14 of those are permanent free tiers rather than expiring trial credits. You sign up with just an email or an existing account, and for most of them the key works immediately with OpenAI-compatible requests.

Free keys do have rate limits. They cap how many [requests you can make per minute and per day](/blog/free-llm-api-rate-limits-compared/), so they suit prototypes and light production, not unlimited scale. For learning, side projects and most apps, a no-card key is enough.

One caution: "no card" offers change. GitHub Models was retired on 2026-07-30, and Cerebras now asks you to add a payment method before it grants $5 of trial credits. Always check the badge on the provider page before you sign up.

## How do you get a free LLM API key step by step?

The process is nearly identical across providers: create an account, open the API keys page, and generate a key. Most providers issue it instantly with no verification beyond an email, so you are calling the model within minutes.

Here is the general flow:

- **Pick a provider** from the [no-card directory](/). Start with one marked "No card" rather than "Phone verification".
- **Sign in** with email or Google. Many skip passwords entirely with social login.
- **Open the API keys page** in the provider console.
- **Generate a key** and copy it immediately, since most show it only once.
- **Store it as an environment variable**, never hard-coded in your source.

Once you have the key, every provider here works the same way through the OpenAI SDK: you just change the base URL. See [what an OpenAI-compatible API is](/blog/openai-compatible-api-guide/) for why that matters.

## Which providers give a free LLM API key the fastest?

**Google Gemini** is the fastest if you already have a Google account: open AI Studio, click to create a key, and you are done, with no new signup at all. **Groq** and **Mistral AI** follow closely, each issuing a key from an email login in under two minutes.

| Provider | Sign in with | Free models listed | Get key |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [Google Gemini](/providers/google_gemini/) | Google account | 3 | aistudio.google.com/app/apikey |
| [Groq](/providers/groq/) | Email / Google | 3 | console.groq.com/keys |
| [Mistral AI](/providers/mistral/) | Email | 4 | console.mistral.ai/api-keys |
| [Cohere](/providers/cohere/) | Email | 5 | dashboard.cohere.com/api-keys |
| [Cloudflare Workers AI](/providers/cloudflare/) | Email | 8 | dash.cloudflare.com/profile/api-tokens |
| [OpenRouter](/providers/openrouter/) | Email | 8 | openrouter.ai/workspaces/default/keys |

Each provider link goes to its live page with the current base URL, models and rate limits. Cloudflare's base URL includes your account ID, so copy that from the dashboard along with the token. Cohere issues a trial key capped at 20 RPM and 1,000 API calls a month, which is fine for testing but not for production traffic.

## How do you use the key once you have it?

Set the key as an environment variable, then point the OpenAI SDK at your provider's base URL. Because these APIs are OpenAI-compatible, the same few lines of code work for any of them. You swap only the base URL, key and model name.

```python
import os
from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI(
    base_url="https://api.groq.com/openai/v1",
    api_key=os.environ["GROQ_API_KEY"],
)
response = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="openai/gpt-oss-120b",
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Explain rate limits in one sentence."}],
)
print(response.choices[0].message.content)
```

Reading the key from `os.environ` keeps it out of your code and out of version control. Never paste a live key into a public repo, because providers scan for leaked keys and revoke them. If you copied an older snippet that calls `llama-3.3-70b-versatile`, switch the model name: that model was removed from Groq's free plan on 2026-08-16.

## What should you avoid when using a free LLM API key?

The biggest mistake is committing a key to a public GitHub repo, which exposes it instantly. The second is hard-coding one key everywhere, so a single rate-limit error takes your whole app down. Both are easy to avoid.

Keep these habits from day one:

- **Store keys in environment variables or a secrets manager**, never in source.
- **Add `.env` to `.gitignore`** before your first commit.
- **Rotate a key immediately** if it ever appears in a log or screenshot.
- **Keep a second provider's key ready** as a fallback when the first hits its limit.

## Which key should a beginner start with?

For a first project, start with **Google Gemini** if you already have a Google account, or **Groq** if you want the fastest responses. Both are no-card, permanent and OpenAI-compatible, so nothing you learn is wasted when you later switch providers.

From there, browse the [full directory of free LLM APIs](/) to match a provider to your use case: [largest context window](/blog/free-llm-api-largest-context-window/), specific open models, or regional availability. The setup you just learned works the same way across all of them.

faq.q: Do any free LLM APIs really need no credit card?
faq.a: Yes. Our directory marks 24 providers that issue a free API key with no credit card (a few are speech or translation APIs), including Groq, Google Gemini, Mistral, Cohere and Cloudflare Workers AI. 14 of them are permanent free tiers rather than expiring trial credits, so you can keep using them within the rate limits.

faq.q: How long does it take to get a free LLM API key?
faq.a: Usually under two minutes. Most providers issue a key instantly after an email or social sign-in. Google Gemini is fastest if you already have a Google account, because you create the key directly in AI Studio without a separate signup.

faq.q: Is GitHub Models or Cerebras still a no-card option?
faq.a: No. GitHub Models was retired on 2026-07-30. Cerebras now requires you to add a payment method, after which it grants $5 of trial credits that expire in 30 days. Groq, Google Gemini and Mistral are the closest no-card alternatives.

faq.q: Is it safe to use a free LLM API key with no credit card?
faq.a: Yes, provided you keep the key private. Store it in an environment variable, add .env to .gitignore, and never commit it to a public repo. Providers actively scan for leaked keys and revoke them, so treat a free key with the same care as a paid one.

faq.q: Can you use one free LLM API key across different tools?
faq.a: Yes. Because these keys work through OpenAI-compatible endpoints, the same key powers any tool that accepts a custom base URL, such as SDKs, coding assistants and chat frontends. You change only the base URL and model name, not the request format.
